newsitem.title: USA: Calif. tax measure creates uncertainty - report.
newsitem.headline: Calif. tax measure creates uncertainty - report.

text.p: A California tax measure approved by voters last week will create an uncertain credit quality environment for general fund-supported leases, lease revenue bonds and other debt obligations, a report concluded.

Underwriter Stone & Youngberg LLC said in its report on Proposition 218 that it does not foresee any municipal insolvencies or lease payment defaults "at this time" for future or existing general fund supported obligations.
"We do however foresee uncertainty for land secured (debt) and other credits supported by a specific tax, assessment, fee or charge," Stone & Youngberg said.
Last week, voters in the state approved the tax measure, which would apply to all cities, counties, special districts, redevelopment agencies and school districts in the state.

Proposition 218 would strengthen existing law to require that all new local taxes be submitted to voters for approval. It would also allow property owners to approve new assessments and strictly limit the use of fees and charges.
